title: Foot technique, parade drummer positions and marching left foot
summary: He plays from the ankle; in the old days drummers marched at the back; marching starts on the left foot like rolls.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: You never do. I just want to say, when you use your leg for beating, do you take your action from your ankle or from your whole leg?

You leave your heel down on the floor and just from your ankle, your toe. Some fellas stomp the whole leg from the hip, you know. Well, I guess it's all how you start off. Yeah, I think they get more tired doing that than just your ankle. Yeah. I really, if I get tired, I really give a single beat until my leg gets rested and I start back in a double beat. Uh-huh. Yeah. That's a good idea. I was going to ask on the parades, in the old days, where did the drummers, where did they march in the parade? Were they at the very back of the band or in the middle or somewhere? Well, they were at the back of the band. It was only later they started. I noticed the Eureka band uses the trumpets in the back. Well, I tell you though, Mr. Russell, I really think it's better. I think it's better. In the middle. In the middle. You know, that's hard in the back.
You have to beat louder, you mean?

No, it's just that the time is harder for you to, you know, get all the instruments together. You have to hear them, hear all of them. The vibrations, when they do boop, that thing's gone, that sound is gone.

Yeah, but see, when you're in the middle like that, you can more sort of have that time to work in just like a clock. Probably easier to hear it. I think so. I think it's better. The way they got it now. But that was a string before. Well, the Eureka is the only one that uses it. The other fellas still do it the old way, I think. I was going to ask too, I know Natty Dominic, you told me a long time ago, they used to always start out with the right foot. When they go one, two, one, two, in marching, the right foot would go back. But in the army bands, they all start at the left foot. That's what I was taught, I was taught in the left foot. You were always taught in the left foot. Before the war, First World War. I see, if you start at your right foot, you're going to make a wrong step. But you take the left foot to start at. And just the same way you're making them rolls. That's what I learned when I was learning how to make a roll. Drop a stick, drop a stick, drop a stick, drop a stick, start at your left hand. And you get the method, the method shows you the left hand. Yeah, I've seen those methods too. You've seen it. And you start like that. And you increase. That push, you know you're making a roll. Oh, oh, oh, oh, see? And just the way with your left foot. In marching, your left foot is the same. Don't swear.
